work.title: Senior Scientist, Translational Data Science
work.summary: I lead single-cell meta-analyses of glial stress across 20+ Parkinson’s, multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer’s cohorts, profiling the astrocyte integrated stress response. This work nominated a patient subgroup carrying almost all of the disease-associated chromatin signal, which helped reframe the target question as “which patients?” I identified a glial stress biomarker for wet-lab validation and showed that the human signature replicates in an in-vitro astrocyte model. I also wrote a four-gate go/no-go framework for evaluating a Parkinson’s therapeutic target, presented findings to program teams and leadership, and built a team tool that runs analysis pipelines on Google Cloud via Cloud Batch and Nextflow.

work.title: Senior Computational Biologist – Spatial/Single-Cell Omics
work.summary: I conducted targeted spatial and single-cell transcriptomics analyses with defined ground truths and known failure modes, enabling rigorous evaluation of AI agent outputs against bioinformatic standards. I designed and implemented reinforcement learning environments, including reward design and task simulators, to train analysis agents, and built evaluation harnesses to benchmark agent robustness, generalization, and reliability across sequencing- and image-based spatial workflows.

work.title: Senior Computational Biologist
work.summary: As a Senior Computational Biologist, I worked at the intersection of biology research and AI/ML model development to build scientific products and scalable computational workflows for biomedical research. I led development of AI Workspace, a no-code platform that streamlines scRNA-seq analysis through automated workflows, integrated AI models, hosted compute, and interactive interfaces. I partnered with scientists, engineers, product teams, and external collaborators, and designed benchmarking and evaluation studies for foundation models and analysis workflows to ensure our products were scientifically valid and usable.

work.title: Computational Biologist (Contract) - OMNI TM
work.summary: As a Computational Biologist on the OMNI Bioinformatics team, I worked within cross-functional teams to support discovery of immunology targets and development of therapeutics for Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD). I developed computational frameworks for the integration and analysis of multimodal data (molecular, cellular, clinical, and imaging) to enhance decision-making across the research and development pipeline, using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, histology, and foundation models for target prioritization and biomarker discovery. As a result, I brought forward two targets for prioritization and created workstreams that reduced dataset analysis time by approximately 10%.

work.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
work.summary: As a postdoctoral researcher, my focus was on computational biology, particularly examining the diverse functions of reactive astrocytes in neurodegeneration. I created a large-scale single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human and mouse astrocytes across neurodegenerative diseases, led the development of analysis pipelines for spatial transcriptomics (10x Visium, 10x Xenium), and built frameworks unifying multi-omics sequencing with CRISPR and ATAC (Perturb-seq, CITE-seq, 10x Multiome). I mentored 3 junior researchers, 1 research associate, and 2 interns.

work.title: Graduate Researcher
work.summary: As a graduate student, I worked on several projects focused on molecular biology and transcriptomics. One project examined glial cells in the spleen and their role in neuroimmune communication during CNS injury. I designed experiments, built RNA-seq workflows in Snakemake, developed Shiny apps for data visualization, analyzed data, and presented the findings at scientific conferences.

work.title: Summer Research Intern
work.summary: During my internship, I gained practical experience in data science and neurology. I explored GABA’s role in decision-making, created MATLAB tasks, and conducted fMRI scans. This experience laid a strong foundation for my career in neurobiology and computational science.
